\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{احتمال} (ehtemâl)}{احتمال (ehtemâl)}]{\fa{احتمال} (ehtemâl) — a probability, a chance}

\label{lesson:FA-C392-ehtemal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for even though, then the Persian for to imagine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{احتمال}}
\textbf{\fa{احتمال}} (\emph{ehtemâl}) — \textquotedblleft{}a probability, a chance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{احتمال} \fa{باران} \fa{امروز} \fa{زیاد} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ehtemâl-e bârân emruz ziyâd ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is a good chance of rain today.
\end{quote}

\emph{Ehtemâl dârad ke} + subjunctive — it is likely that. The adverb is \emph{ehtemâlan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{احتمال}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{iḥtimāl} \textquotedblleft{}likelihood, what can be borne\textquotedblright{}, on the root \emph{ḥ-m-l} \textquotedblleft{}to carry\textquotedblright{}, the same source as \emph{ehtemâlan} \textquotedblleft{}probably\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ehtemâl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ehtemâl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ehtemâl}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for even though, then the Persian for to imagine, then say \emph{ehtemâl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{احتمال} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A probability, a chance\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{احتمال} \fa{دادن} (ehtemâl dâdan)}{احتمال دادن (ehtemâl dâdan)}]{\fa{احتمال} \fa{دادن} (ehtemâl dâdan) — to think likely, to suspect}

\label{lesson:FA-C392-ehtemal-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to imagine, then the Persian for a probability.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{احتمال} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{احتمال} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{ehtemâl dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to think likely, to suspect\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{من} \fa{احتمال} \fa{میدهم} \fa{که} \fa{او} \fa{دیر} \fa{بیاید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{man ehtemâl midaham ke u dir biyâyad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I think he will probably come late.
\end{quote}

\emph{Ehtemâl} + \emph{dâdan} (stem \emph{deh-}); \emph{ke} + subjunctive follows.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{احتمال} \fa{دادن}} is literally \textquotedblleft{}to give a likelihood\textquotedblright{}: \emph{ehtemâl} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{iḥtimāl}, and \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{} is traced by EtymDB to PIE \emph{deh\textsubscript{3}-}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ehtemâl dâdan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ehtemâl dâdan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to imagine, then the Persian for a probability, then say \emph{ehtemâl dâdan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{امکان} (emkân)}{امکان (emkân)}]{\fa{امکان} (emkân) — a possibility; a facility}

\label{lesson:FA-C392-emkan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a probability, then the Persian for to think likely.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{امکان}}
\textbf{\fa{امکان}} (\emph{emkân}) — \textquotedblleft{}a possibility; a facility\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{امکان} \fa{دارد} \fa{که} \fa{فردا} \fa{برف} \fa{بیاید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{emkân dârad ke fardâ barf biyâyad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
It may snow tomorrow.
\end{quote}

\emph{Emkân dârad ke} + subjunctive — it is possible that. Plural \emph{emkânât}, facilities.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{امکان}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{imkān} \textquotedblleft{}possibility\textquotedblright{}, from the same Arabic family as \emph{mumkin}, the source of Persian \emph{momken} \textquotedblleft{}possible\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بعید} (ba'id)}{بعید (ba'id)}]{\fa{بعید} (ba'id) — unlikely; far-fetched}

\label{lesson:FA-C392-baid}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to think likely, then the Persian for a possibility.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بعید}}
\textbf{\fa{بعید}} (\emph{ba'id}) — \textquotedblleft{}unlikely; far-fetched\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بعید} \fa{است} \fa{که} \fa{او} \fa{امروز} \fa{بیاید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ba'id ast ke u emruz biyâyad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
It is unlikely that he will come today.
\end{quote}

\emph{Ba'id ast ke} + subjunctive. Its first meaning is \textquotedblleft{}far\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{بعید}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{ba'īd} \textquotedblleft{}far, remote\textquotedblright{}: an unlikely thing is far from happening.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{قطعی} (qat'i)}{قطعی (qat'i)}]{\fa{قطعی} (qat'i) — definite, final}

\label{lesson:FA-C392-qati}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a possibility, then the Persian for unlikely.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{قطعی}}
\textbf{\fa{قطعی}} (\emph{qat'i}) — \textquotedblleft{}definite, final\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{تاریخ} \fa{سفر} \fa{هنوز} \fa{قطعی} \fa{نیست}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{târikh-e safar hanuz qat'i nist.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The date of the trip is not definite yet.
\end{quote}

From \emph{qat'} \textquotedblleft{}cutting\textquotedblright{} + \emph{-i}: a cut-and-dried decision.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{قطعی}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{qaṭ'ī} \textquotedblleft{}decisive\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{qaṭ'} \textquotedblleft{}cutting\textquotedblright{}: a definite answer cuts off doubt.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
